decisive_items: sphenoid ostium was obstructed by a pyocele, which was marsupialized and drained
Histopathology was negative for hyphae and neoplastic cells, and cultures grew no bacteria or fungi
T2-weighted images showed a markedly hypointense signal in the lateral recess with peripheral mucosal inflammation
response.rationale: Surgical identification of an obstructing pyocele, negative fungal and neoplastic histopathology, and T2-hypointense inspissated sinus contents are most consistent with a sphenoid sinus mucocele/pyocele; the invasive imaging findings reflect erosion and inflammation rather than tumor or fungal invasion.

rejected.why: Chronic invasive fungal sinusitis can mimic bone erosion and T2 hypointensity, but histopathology was negative for hyphae and cultures grew no fungi, while a marsupialized pyocele was found.
Tolosa-Hunt syndrome would be steroid-responsive cavernous inflammation, but prednisone provided no benefit and surgery confirmed an obstructing pyocele with purulent discharge.
Trigeminal schwannoma could explain V2/V3 and cavernous sinus involvement, but histopathology was negative for neoplastic cells and the operative finding of a pyocele strongly favors mucocele.
